source.title: Major open problems in chaos theory and nonlinear dynamics

accepted.question_text: Find an effective description of chaos and turbulence, especially turbulence arising under the Navier-Stokes flow, that is mathematically meaningful and practically useful rather than merely formal. Existing candidates mentioned in the source include Reynolds averaging, fractal dimension, SRB measures, horseshoes, and shadowing, but the source states that Reynolds averaging leads to an unsolvable closure problem for chaos and turbulence, fractal dimension lacks engineering value, SRB measures are elusive for most systems, and shadowing the entire turbulent attractor is still beyond current computational reach. The question is therefore what kind of averaging or other description can faithfully capture chaotic and turbulent dynamics in a way that is effective for engineering use.
accepted.context_brief: Effective description of turbulence and chaos

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence

More specifically, the mechanism of how chaotic dynamics operates is understood; how to effectively describe chaos in term of some sort of averaging is beyond reach (i.e. not tamed); it is not even clear what kind of averaging mean we should be after for! These questions will form the first major open problem to be discussed below.
A description of turbulence which is effective in engineering means a solution of the problem of turbulence.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether violent turbulence at sufficiently high Reynolds number is caused primarily by rough dependence on initial data rather than by the usual sensitive dependence on initial data associated with chaos. In the source, rough dependence means that arbitrarily small perturbations of the initial condition can reach order-one size essentially instantly, as suggested by the behavior of the Euler solution map, whereas sensitive dependence means exponential growth of perturbations over a nonzero accumulation time. The question is whether high-Reynolds-number Navier-Stokes dynamics inherit this rough-dependence mechanism strongly enough that it explains the short-time onset and violence of turbulence.
accepted.context_brief: Rough versus sensitive dependence in turbulence

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data
My conjecture is that the high Reynolds number violent turbulence is due to such rough dependence on initial data, rather than sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos.

In summary, not large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos, while large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to rough dependence on initial data.

accepted.question_text: For the cosmological arrow of time, if the velocities of every object or every molecule in the universe were simultaneously reversed, would the universe still continue expanding? This asks whether macroscopic time asymmetry can persist under microscopic velocity reversal, and therefore whether chaos theory is relevant not only to the thermodynamic arrow of time but also to the cosmological arrow of time.
accepted.context_brief: Arrow of time and velocity reversal

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data, 3. arrow of time

For the cosmological arrow of time, one may ask the question: Is the universe still expanding if the velocity of every object (or every molecule) is simultaneously reversed? If the answer is yes, then chaos theory may still be relevant.

accepted.question_text: Is the paradox of enrichment a genuine experimentally observable ecological phenomenon, in which increasing the nutrient-driven carrying capacity of a prey population can lead to extinction of both prey and predator, or is it merely an artifact of a particular class of predator-prey mathematical models? If it is only a modeling artifact, then the underlying question becomes how to formulate better mathematical models that do not produce this spurious prediction while still capturing the ecological dynamics.
accepted.context_brief: Experimental reality of the paradox of enrichment

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data, 3. arrow of time, 4. the paradox of enrichment

The most important question is whether or not this paradox can be observed experimentally. It is possible that the paradox is purely an artifact of the mathematical models, while in reality increasing the nutrition to the prey never leads to an extinction. If that is the case, then developing better mathematical models is necessary.

accepted.question_text: Explain the paradox of plankton by constructing a mathematically and physically adequate model in which many species of phytoplankton can coexist while competing for only one or a few limiting nutrients in a turbulent fluid environment. The source frames the paradox as the tension between competitive exclusion, which suggests that only one or a few species should survive at equilibrium under a small number of limiting resources, and the observed coexistence of hundreds of plankton species. The open problem is to identify a dynamics, likely involving both ecological interactions and chaotic fluid transport, that accounts for this coexistence.
accepted.context_brief: Coexistence in the paradox of plankton

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data, 3. arrow of time, 4. the paradox of enrichment, 5. the paradox of pesticides, 6. the paradox of plankton.

According to the principle of competitive exclusion, the final equilibrium state should be taken over by one or a few species according to the limiting factors. On the other hand, in reality hundreds species of the plankton coexist. This paradoxical question was first raised by Hutchinson [7].
Since Hutchinson’s work, there have been many studies on the paradox [27]. The problem involves two branches of chaotic dynamics: fluids and ecology.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The paradox of pesticides says that pesticides may dramatically increase the population of a pest when the pest has a natural predator. ... To guide the application of pesticide in such a circumstance, a good mathematical model will be important.

evidence.quote: Unlike the paradox of enrichment, the paradox of pesticides was observed in experiments [5] [4] [12].
To guide the application of pesticide in such a circumstance, a good mathematical model will be important. From the perspective of mathematical models, the phenomenon can be easily understood [18].
